conventions.convention: Time starts at zero; boundary crossing is tested at positive integer times using S_t ≥ u(V_t). Scale c is strictly positive in the boundary definition.

For each λ separately, exponential domination is by a nonnegative integrable adapted supermartingale with initial expectation at most one. Joint measurability in λ is not required by the pair definition.
Confidence intervals are closed, have finite measurable endpoints, and simultaneously cover an adapted, possibly random and time-varying target under the specified law.
Forecasts are measurable before their corresponding observations. V_t is the observed sum of squared forecast errors, not a predictable conditional-variance process.
The zero-range branch a=b returns [a,a]; otherwise the two-sided error δ is allocated as α=δ/2 to each one-sided crossing event.
AC is assumed. Conditional means may use any real measurable versions; the target is their running average, and coverage is invariant under these choices.
A diagonal-only matrix rule has auxiliary randomness whose law is independent of r, and its radii are almost surely finite.

load_bearing.statement: Under AC, bounded adapted observations X_t ∈ [a,b], predictable forecasts in [a,b], and a Borel scale-(b−a) one-sided boundary at error δ/2, the algorithm's intervals simultaneously cover the running average conditional means with probability at least 1−δ. The zero-range case returns [a,a]; coverage is independent of conditional-expectation versions. Positive finite mixtures with 0<λ_j<1/c and weights summing to one supply boundaries through the stated unique nonnegative root equation.

For α ∈ (0,1), a Borel function u:[0,∞)→[0,∞) is a scale-c one-sided sub-exponential uniform boundary if every scale-c pair satisfying the stated exponential supermartingale-domination condition obeys P(∃t≥1:S_t≥u(V_t))≤α.
If c=0, return C_t=[a,a]. If c>0, update the sample mean and V_t=V_{t−1}+(X_t−forecast_t)², then return the closed interval centered at the sample mean with radius u_{δ/2,c}(V_t)/t.
A sequence of random closed intervals with finite adapted endpoints is a (1−α) confidence sequence for an adapted real target process θ_t if P(θ_t∈C_t for every t≥1)≥1−α.
